criteria_for_a_good_query: Plausible: a real video editor working with this corpus would type this exact string. Not formal, not cherry-picked.
Grounded: the speakers, topics, formats, and time windows refer to things actually present in the Hormozi/Sharran corpus (verified against topic_segments.json, audio_tags.json, scene_tags.json).
Decidable: there's a clear definition of what a 'good match' looks like — we can score each top-5 result yes/no on whether it satisfies the query.
Diverse: covers single-dim (just topic, just speaker, just visual, just time) and multi-dim (combinations). Mix of short and verbose, formal and casual.
Includes friction: at least 10 queries that broke the regex-and-list approach (prepositional phrases, ellipses, ambiguous nouns, missing verbs).
Not biased: I do NOT know in advance which system will do better on each query. Don't construct queries to favor the new design.

what_a_good_result_means.speaker_correctness: If the query specifies a speaker, the result's voice (audio classifier) must match. Deterministic from data.
what_a_good_result_means.time_correctness: If the query specifies a time window, the result's recency_days must satisfy it. Deterministic from data.
what_a_good_result_means.visual_correctness: If the query asks for a visual format the classifier covers (animation, talking_head_pose), the tag must match. For visual concepts outside the classifier (whiteboard, B-roll, etc.), we trust the LLM judge's eyes-closed assessment of whether CLIP retrieval is plausible — graded on rubric.
what_a_good_result_means.topic_correctness: If the query has a topic ask, the transcript content must address it. LLM judge with 0/1/2 rubric: 2=directly addresses, 1=tangentially mentions, 0=unrelated.
what_a_good_result_means.overall: A result is 'good' iff every specified dimension scores correct (visual is best-effort). precision@5 = fraction of top-5 that are good.
